messages.content: Return only JSON with keys decomposition,systemd,disconnect,shutdown,firstPatch. Review this proposed Node.js change: extract the current stdin/stdout service's scheduler+journal+replay state into createInferenceBroker(); keep serve-inference-jsonl as a thin session; add serve-inference-socket using node:net with either --socket PATH or systemd LISTEN_FDS fd 3; each accepted connection parses bounded NDJSON and serializes only that connection's results; accepted jobs survive disconnect and remain journaled for ID replay; socket clients cannot send shutdown control; SIGTERM stops listening, stops scheduler admission, drains accepted jobs, then closes. One process lock remains keyed by journal. Identify the exact ownership decomposition, correct systemd fd handling, disconnect behavior, shutdown order, and the smallest first patch that avoids duplicating scheduler state. Under 1400 characters total.

completion.text: {"decomposition":"Broker owns: scheduler queue, journal fd, replay index (jobId→result). Sessions own only transport I/O. serve-inference-jsonl reads stdin, calls broker.submit(), pipes results to stdout. serve-inference-socket accepts connections; each socket registers per-jobId result listeners with the broker and writes back on emit; broker itself never holds socket references.","systemd":"Check LISTEN_PID===String(process.pid) && +LISTEN_FDS>=1; if so, server.listen({fd:3}), else server.listen(socketPath). Never call listen() twice. Node won't auto-close inherited fds; rely on process.exit() or close fd 3 explicitly before exit.","disconnect":"On socket end/error, deregister its result listeners from the broker. In-flight jobs continue and journal normally; no results delivered to gone sockets. No in-memory buffer for disconnected clients. Replay is available on reconnect via broker.replay(jobId).","shutdown":"SIGTERM: (1) server.close() — no new accepts; (2) broker.stopAdmission() — new submit() calls rejected; (3) await broker.drain() — in-flight jobs finish and journal; (4) socket.end() all open connections; (5) close journal fd; (6) exit.","firstPatch":"Extract scheduler, journal fd, and replay Map from serve-inference-jsonl into inferencebroker.js; export createInferenceBroker()→{submit,replay,stopAdmission,drain}. Rewire serve-inference-jsonl to use it. No behavior change, no socket code yet. One broker instance shared across future entry points — no state duplication possible."}

structured_output.decomposition: Broker owns: scheduler queue, journal fd, replay index (jobId→result). Sessions own only transport I/O. serve-inference-jsonl reads stdin, calls broker.submit(), pipes results to stdout. serve-inference-socket accepts connections; each socket registers per-jobId result listeners with the broker and writes back on emit; broker itself never holds socket references.
structured_output.systemd: Check LISTEN_PID===String(process.pid) && +LISTEN_FDS>=1; if so, server.listen({fd:3}), else server.listen(socketPath). Never call listen() twice. Node won't auto-close inherited fds; rely on process.exit() or close fd 3 explicitly before exit.
structured_output.disconnect: On socket end/error, deregister its result listeners from the broker. In-flight jobs continue and journal normally; no results delivered to gone sockets. No in-memory buffer for disconnected clients. Replay is available on reconnect via broker.replay(jobId).
structured_output.shutdown: SIGTERM: (1) server.close() — no new accepts; (2) broker.stopAdmission() — new submit() calls rejected; (3) await broker.drain() — in-flight jobs finish and journal; (4) socket.end() all open connections; (5) close journal fd; (6) exit.
